item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E002","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"World Bank WITS reported Egypt's 2023 trade indicators as a Hirschman-Herfindahl market-concentration index of 0.04, export-market penetration index of 0.04, world growth of 0.04%, and Egypt country growth of -9.03%; it also reported 2023 service imports of about $22.006 billion, service exports of $33.649 billion, and imports of goods and services equal to 21.34% of GDP.","notes":["The supplied excerpt ends before the exports-of-goods-and-services percentage, so the claimed 19.11% is unsupported."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Egypt's nuclear regulator issued a construction licence for El Dabaa unit 3 on 31 March 2023 after a comprehensive site inspection from 11 to 17 March; the Nuclear Power Plants Authority stated that the licensing documents met regulatory requirements and achieved high nuclear-safety standards.","notes":["The excerpt attributes the statement about meeting requirements and safety standards to the Nuclear Power Plants Authority, not jointly to the regulator and project authority."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"An Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights analysis published on 28 March 2023 reported that currency devaluations, austerity, reduced public spending, higher service prices, and debt-increasing economic policy agreed and coordinated with the IMF contributed to severe inflation; it reported consumer-price inflation at a five-year high in February and core inflation at 40%, while noting that the lowest-income group spent about 47% of expenditure on food.","notes":["The excerpt specifies the lowest-income group, not poor households generally."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0015-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
